method: One uninterrupted open-loop stage of tools/k8s/api_load.py's generator at a constant arrival rate (request i is due at t0 + i/rate whatever the outstanding requests; latency = intended start to end of the response, failures counted at their latency), against the NodePort 127.0.0.1:18376 across the 3 API pods, on a database of ~1.04M cases / 7.2M events, while the 2 scheduler pods (one leads) sweep every 10 s with the automation and evidence scans, and the watchdog runs its scan (M7-7: the incremental scan plus a slice of the full reconciliation pass) at the chart's interval (watchdog.intervalSeconds). The mix is api_load.py's (bounded worklist only: GET /cases?state=lost_contact). Every 60 s a sampler records per-pod cgroup memory (memory.current and anon from memory.stat) and CPU (kubectl exec; no metrics-server), container restart counts and last-termination reasons (kubectl get pods), the database size, the scheduler leader lease and the heartbeats table, and reads the new log lines of the API, scheduler and watchdog pods. Restarts during the soak = restartCount at the last sample minus at the first sample (pre-existing restarts excluded). Memory growth = least-squares slope of the pod's memory.current (and of anon) over the soak; reported for the whole series and for the series after the first 20 minutes (after caches and the allocator have warmed up); a pod that restarted has its series cut at the restart (the slope is taken over its longest restart-free stretch). Sweeps expected = measured seconds / 10 (the nominal interval; the real period is interval + the loop's own work: drain, sweep, automation scan, evidence scan, which run in series). Sweep duration = time between the outbox-drain and sweep access-log lines on the API (the sweep runs between them). Watchdog scan duration = from the instant the watchdog starts the call (its start, or its previous outcome + interval) to the API's access-log line for POST /watchdog/scan (logged when the request ends); the watchdog's own HTTP client times out after 120 s and logs 'scan failed', but the API goes on with the scan until it finishes. The generator, the kind cluster and Postgres share one host.
chart_file_values_kind:
# Local kind cluster `sc-m76` (M7-6 scalability evidence, re-measured in M7-7): `make k8s-up` installs the chart with this file.
# Everything else is the chart's production defaults. DEVIATIONS FROM PRODUCTION, and why:
#  1. images: local tag `m76`, built from this working tree and loaded with `kind load docker-image` (pullPolicy Never): no registry.
#  2. replicas: api 3, scheduler 2, watchdog 1 (the benchmark topology; production default api is 2). api cpu limit "1", memory
#     request 256Mi: the Docker VM is ~8 GB shared with the compose stack, three 1 GiB-limit API pods plus Postgres do not fit.
#  3. Identity: APP_ENV stays `production`, so ALL of secure_config_problems() still applies (oidc mode, no dev login,
#     wall clock, 32-byte distinct tokens). The issuer is the placeholder https://idp.kind.invalid/realms/sc-m76 and the API
#     fetches its signing keys from OIDC_JWKS_URL = the in-cluster `sc-jwks` pod (plain HTTP, tools/k8s/jwks.yaml) instead of an
#     identity provider. Tokens are minted by tools/k8s/mint_token.py with a throw-away RSA key (Secret sc-oidc-signing). Production
#     signing keys live at the IdP; here whoever can read that Secret can mint any role, including supervisor.
#  4. FHIR: there is NO FHIR server in the cluster (no HAPI image is approved). fhirVerifyEvidence stays "true" because the API
#     refuses to start otherwise; it only matters on `close`, whose evidence_ref lookup will therefore FAIL here (HTTP error from
#     the verifier). Do not close cases in this cluster. fhirProjection is "false" (production default "true"): with it on every
#     event would queue for a server that does not exist and end in dead letters. fhirBaseUrl is an unresolvable placeholder.
#  5. Database: in-cluster plain Postgres 16 (tools/k8s/postgres.yaml), no TLS (sslmode=disable in the generated DSNs), no HA, no
#     backups, a 5 Gi local-path volume. Production: managed server with sslmode=require.
#  6. Secrets are generated by tools/k8s/up.sh into Kubernetes Secrets (nothing committed); `secrets.create` stays false.
#  7. API Service is NodePort 30076, published on 127.0.0.1:18376 by kind-config.yaml; no ingress. Probes/NetworkPolicy as in production.
#  8. NetworkPolicy: rendered and applied, but kind's default CNI (kindnet) does NOT enforce it (tested: a pod under the
#     default-deny policy still reached Postgres). The rules are therefore unverified here, and the benchmark measures a cluster
#     without enforcement overhead. The database CIDR is the pod range of kind-config.yaml (10.244.0.0/16), the host-side
#     ingress range is the docker network of the nodes (set by up.sh).
#  9. OTLP off, logFormat json (as production), CORS empty, leaderLeaseTtlSeconds 30 and requireLeaderFence true (as production).
images:
  api:       { repository: screening-closure-api,       tag: m76, pullPolicy: Never }
  scheduler: { repository: screening-closure-scheduler, tag: m76, pullPolicy: Never }
  watchdog:  { repository: screening-closure-watchdog,  tag: m76, pullPolicy: Never }

api:
  replicas: 3
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: 250m, memory: 256Mi }
    limits:   { cpu: "1",  memory: 768Mi }
  sweepWorkers: "1"          # single-process sweeps: one CPU per pod; raise together with the cpu limit
  service: { type: NodePort, port: 8000, nodePort: 30076 }

scheduler:
  replicas: 2

# M7-7: the watchdog and the agency run at the PRODUCTION settings here (no override). M7-6 had to slow the watchdog to 900 s (its scan
# replayed every open case: 224-230 s at ~1M) and switch the agency off (its pass read the whole case table and OOM-killed an API pod).
# Both are bounded now (ADR-045; app.agency.tools), so `watchdog.intervalSeconds` and `app.agencyEverySweeps` come from values.yaml.
watchdog:
  replicas: 1

app:
  env: production
  oidcIssuer: https://idp.kind.invalid/realms/sc-m76
  oidcJwksUrl: http://sc-jwks:8080/jwks.json
  fhirBaseUrl: http://fhir.invalid/fhir
  fhirVerifyEvidence: "true"
  fhirProjection: "false"

networkPolicy:
  enabled: true
  dnsNamespaceLabels: { kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system }
  ingressFrom: []
  metricsFrom: []
  ingressCidrs: ["172.16.0.0/12"]       # overridden by up.sh with the kind docker network's subnet
  egress:
    database: { cidr: 10.244.0.0/16, port: 5432 }   # the in-cluster Postgres pod (kind pod range)
    fhir:     { cidr: "", port: 443 }               # no FHIR server here
    oidc:     { cidr: "", port: 443 }               # the JWKS pod is reached through `extra`
    otlp:     { cidr: "", port: 4318 }
    extra:
      - to:
          - podSelector: { matchLabels: { app: sc-jwks } }
        ports: [{ protocol: TCP, port: 8080 }]

# M7-8: the cluster runs the chart's defaults for the new settings too (no override above): the scheduler's four timed tasks (10/10/10/60 s),
# api.maxInflightRequests 40 per pod (503 + Retry-After above it), app.agencyOwnCadence "true", metricsRefreshBudgetSeconds 3, one uvicorn worker.
# The mitigation A/B of docs/results/scale.md sets api.server.workers=2 and limitMaxRequests on the command line (helm --set), not here.

summary.criteria: p99 (answered requests, from intended start) < 500 ms and error rate (not counting refusals) < 0.1%; refusals (503 + Retry-After) are reported apart; without_shedding additionally needs zero refusals
